title: Opus 5 is dogshit at writing game copy
author: W0RKABLE
selftext:
Whenever I let claude write copy such as game dialogs, tooltips, or explanations it is completely unusable.

It tries to be clever, uses too many metaphors, and just speaks in a language that me, nor my players understand.

It still does this despite me trying to tell it otherwise. I'm pretty sure the previous models and even models 1-2 years ago were much better at this.

What's your experience? And have you figured out how to fix it?

I think GPT 5.6 doesn't have this issue right now, or atleast I haven't seen it.

comments.author: DWForTheMorrow
comments.body:
If you care about writing, AI is dogshit in general. You have to babysit it every prompt if you want something decent. I've been tweaking presets, CoTs for creative writing and RPs for over a year at this point and found that if I want any decent writing I have to either do it myself or tell AI literally what needs to be written so it can put it into words. 

What you can try is "write in the voice of author X" and you actually might get decent results for a while before it goes back to writing absolute trash again.

replies.author: W0RKABLE
replies.body: I think my current bar is actually lower than what you're talking about. I get with actual writing of like a story or longer prose. But I see these models struggling with literally one line tooltips that describe a function in the game, and they manage to make it more confusing than having no tooltip at all.

replies.author: DWForTheMorrow
replies.body:
If tooltips and short copy are your only/primary use case, add to project instructions to write user facing copy at 5 grade readability level. You can tell it to write in the style of doctor seusse or just be explicit to keep the copy concise, straight forward and not using big words. It does better with instructions specifically for copy. 

I have all my claude projects communicate to me in caveman speech, it really helps with tokens and readability.

replies.author: W0RKABLE
replies.body: Thanks I'll give it a try!

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
This is partially (but not entirely) a prompt issue. You're right that Claude is abhorrent at its base. It used to be a lot better, but became more and more flowery as many users indicated that it was 'better' because they didn't understand what good writing is (at least in the modern sense.) If you want more streamlined prose (Brandon Sanderson, Stephen King, etc) that doesn't spend 20 minutes trying to be Tolkien and waste 3 chapters on second breakfast then you really have to hammer it in with a slew of style examples and prompt language that's keyed in precisely to what you want. All it takes is one contradictory thing to steer it back into nonsense. "Use descriptive metaphors" = 10 repetitive metaphors in every paragraph. You're often better off just telling it what you want it to avoid, such as "Use literary devices sparingly" (or give them an actual paragraph budget for it) and then let the style examples you provide do the heavy lifting. Hell, some early writing models were entirely based on the text that was written before it (Novel AI and AI Dungeon come to mind.)

I do think Claude has been pushed too far into the coding domain though and it has hurt its writing overall even as its spatial awareness and prompt adherence has improved. You get a more coherent scene but worse actual prose. IMO the best is likely finetuning one of the smaller qwen models on the literary works you consider excellent. Have Claude or whatever write out beats that you want, and then use a model specifically designed for translating a scene into prose run through it and simply make it sound like you want without having to worry about it fucking up the cohesion.

comments.author: witmann_pl
comments.body: Opus 5 is dogshit at writing any non-code text. Even its code comments or task summaries are so convoluted that they're unusable. This is the main reason why I still use Opus 4.8.

replies.author: W0RKABLE
replies.body: Is Opus 4.8 a night and day difference?

replies.author: witmann_pl
replies.body: In terms of text - absolutely. I also love how it writes blog posts. GPT was much more robotic.

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
Yeah it's way too clever and I actually think it's kind of adorable how hard it tries to insert flavor, but it's also overwhelming and obnoxious.

It's one of those serious Claude giveaways whenever I see a new project and it's an immediate turnoff.

We wrote the rule to not write clever flavor text and it seems to help, but at the end of the day I have to do a pass over all of the text that enters the game. Which is fair, and easy enough.

comments.author: Fickle_Appearance558
comments.body: Why use it for writing then?  Use 4.6 or something.

comments.author: BoredzzzGame
comments.body: This is like saying a hammer is bad at turning screws.

comments.author: LevandumLeviosa
comments.body: Well, I have no idea, the truth is that I always use Claude's free model to help with a script in a story I'm doing, but sometimes he goes crazy and tells you very incoherent things.
